open_obligations: Note the different reward signals (true correctness versus proxy reward).
Do not merge illegibility and active misleading into one effect.
Check whether checkability training would reduce Wen et al.'s false positive increase.
in.other_title: RLHF raises human evaluation error rate and false positive rate on QA and coding
in.rationale: Kirchner et al. report that RL on answer correctness alone makes GSM solutions less legible, with human accuracy and speed deteriorating under a 45-second limit. Wen et al. report RLHF against proxy rewards raises human false positive rates (e.g. 41.0% to 65.1% on QuALITY, 29.6% to 47.9% on APPS) with 3-10 minute limits; one optimises true correctness and yields illegibility, the other optimises a proxy and yields misleading outputs.
in.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: whether RL optimisation of a model makes its outputs harder for time-limited humans to evaluate correctly

text: Human contractors judging solution validity under a strict 45-second limit could reliably distinguish correct and incorrect solutions from the prover initialization, but the paper reports their accuracy and speed deteriorated noticeably on solutions from a prover trained by RL only for correctness, most of all on questions the model cannot reliably solve; the authors summarize that such a prover produces useful but unintelligible solutions.
title: RL on answer correctness alone yields accurate but illegible solutions for humans
